title: The Ghost of the DMZ
premise: Ansel Iversen, a fixer for a deniable diplomatic unit operating along the Korean DMZ, has spent two years burying the memory of a night operation that went wrong. When a stranger named Yuna arrives claiming Ansel once saved her life — a favor Ansel never performed — she brings evidence that the 'incident' was not an accident but a sanctioned massacre, and that the man who ordered it now sits on the extraction committee deciding who leaves the peninsula at dawn. Hunted by three governments and a ghost-faced assassin who only kills witnesses, Ansel must choose between protecting the embassy that owns her and delivering the truth to a journalist on the last flight out. She gets the file aboard, exposes the commander at cost of her own immunity, and walks away from the DMZ finally able to sleep.
about_author: Ines Montrose is a former conflict-zone translator who spent six years working along border regions before turning to fiction. She writes thrillers about people trapped between institutions and their consciences.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Happened
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Insomnia-ridden in Seoul, she handles a routine disposal of a diplomat's indiscretions until a woman named Yuna corners her with a photograph Ansel doesn't remember taking — proof of a debt owed. The beat: unease disguised as professional calm.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: Yuna reveals she carries a drive containing logs from Nightfall, the operation Ansel buried. Ansel denies everything, but recognizes the kill-chain signatures. POV shifts briefly to Yuna: she isn't blackmailing; she's repaying. Beat: denial cracking into dread.

chapters.title: The Embassy That Isn't
chapters.summary: Ansel reports the approach to her handler, Merrick, inside the unlisted annex. He orders her to identify Yuna's sources and nothing more. Ansel notices his hands shaking. Beat: loyalty tested by a handler who fears his own institution.

chapters.title: Ghost-Face
chapters.summary: Assassin's POV, unnamed. A witness in Incheon dies quietly; we learn the assassin works from a ledger of names connected to Nightfall, crossing them off for a client he's never met. Beat: cold procedural menace, first real stakes.

chapters.title: Yuna's Ledger
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Against orders she meets Yuna again and reads the drive: coordinates, timestamps, and her own callsign on the comms log. The favor was fabricated to get close to her — but the evidence is real. Beat: vertigo of discovering you were chosen, not found.

chapters.title: Three Governments
chapters.summary: Dual POV. American, South Korean, and Chinese liaison officers each learn fragments exist; each wants the drive silenced for different reasons. Ansel realizes there is no safe handoff. Beat: claustrophobia as every exit closes.

chapters.title: The Safehouse Rule
chapters.summary: Ansel stashes Yuna in a decommissioned listening post she alone remembers. They trade histories; Yuna's brother died at Nightfall. Ansel admits she was on comms that night and heard the order given. Beat: guilt spoken aloud for the first time.

chapters.title: Merrick's Bargain
chapters.summary: Merrick offers Ansel immunity and a transfer if she surrenders the drive. She stalls, then finds a second copy already missing from the annex — someone inside is feeding the assassin. Beat: betrayal reframes the enemy.

chapters.title: Crossing at Dusk
chapters.summary: Ansel and Yuna move north under cover of a joint inspection convoy to reach the surviving Nightfall radio operator. Assassin's POV interleave: he is one step behind, patient. Beat: road-trip tension, trust forming under fire.

chapters.title: The Man in the Bunker
chapters.summary: The old operator, half-mad, confirms the order came from Colonel Voss — now the committee chair controlling dawn extraction. He gives Ansel the original authentication codes. Beat: the past made flesh; hope with a price tag.

chapters.title: Compromised
chapters.summary: The safehouse burns behind them; the assassin missed them by minutes because someone warned him. Ansel deduces the leak is Deputy Chief Aldridge, who ran Nightfall logistics. Beat: paranoia sharpening into certainty.

chapters.title: What Voss Bought
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Ansel's fragmented memory of Nightfall finally assembling: civilians in a cross-border tunnel, an order to sanitize, her own silence afterward. Beat: the theme of inheritance — she inherited the cover-up the moment she stayed quiet.

chapters.title: A Journalist Named Okonkwo
chapters.summary: Ansel contacts Adaeze Okonkwo, the only reporter with clearance to board the dawn flight. Okonkwo agrees to carry the story but demands verification within twelve hours. Beat: the plan crystallizes; the clock starts.

chapters.title: The Committee Room
chapters.summary: Ansel walks into the extraction committee under a diplomatic pretext and faces Voss across the table. He recognizes her, offers her a future in exchange for forgetting. Beat: power's corruption offered politely, face to face.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Ansel declines and walks out knowing she's marked. Merrick covers her exit at personal ruin, revealing he lost a son at Nightfall too. Beat: unexpected alliance; grief as fuel.

chapters.title: Trap at the Terminal
chapters.summary: Yuna is taken at Gimpo while running decoy. Assassin's POV: he hesitates — his ledger lists Yuna as a source, not a target, and his client's orders have changed. Beat: the instrument begins questioning the hand.

chapters.title: The Assassin's Client
chapters.summary: The assassin traces payment routing to Aldridge, not Voss — Aldridge ordered Nightfall and has been erasing everyone, including Voss's trail. He delivers this to Ansel instead of killing her. Beat: justice outside the law, from an unlikely hand.

chapters.title: Exchange at the Bridge
chapters.summary: Ansel trades herself for Yuna at Freedom Bridge, buying time with the authentication codes as leverage over both governments. Beat: sacrifice as strategy; the theme of debt paid forward.

chapters.title: Dawn Extraction
chapters.summary: Climax. On the tarmac, Ansel confronts Voss and Aldridge before the flight boards, broadcasting the verified logs to Okonkwo mid-confrontation. The assassin appears — and puts his final bullet into Aldridge's escape plan, not Ansel. Beat: truth forced past every gate at once.

chapters.title: Aftermath in Daylight
chapters.summary: Voss arrested by his own committee to contain damage; the story breaks globally before it can be buried. Ansel loses her immunity, her employer, and her anonymity. Beat: victory that costs everything except the point.

chapters.title: What She Inherited
chapters.summary: Quiet epilogue-adjacent chapter. Ansel and Yuna scatter the Nightfall dead's names at the DMZ fence line. Merrick sends one message: run. Beat: mourning turned into inheritance — the names now belong to her.

chapters.title: Sleep
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Ansel's POV, months later in Reykjavik under a new name. Okonkwo's series runs; a postcard arrives unsigned with a single crossed-out name. Ansel sleeps through the night. Beat: resolution — peace earned, vigilance kept.
